chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Ghurrah, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever visits his brother for the sake of Allah, during illness or health, not coming to him for deception nor for reciprocal exchange, Allah will assign to him seventy thousand angels who will call out behind him:
You have done well, and Paradise is made better for you, for you are visitors of Allah, and you are a delegation of the Beneficent,
until he arrives at his house.'

So Yūsayr said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! And even if the place is distant?' He said: 'Yes, O Yūsayr, and even if the place is a year's journey, for Allah is Generous and the angels are numerous; they will escort him until he returns to his house.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother in faith for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish ziyarat al-akhin as a profound act of worship that transcends physical proximity, with the Imam affirming that even a year's journey yields the same reward because Allah is Generous. The presence of seventy thousand angels serving as witnesses underscores the divine validation of this social bond, framing the visitor as the 'deputation of the Merciful' who maintains the spiritual network of the Ummah. This tradition is often cited by Shia jurists to emphasize that the intention of sincerity (ikhlas) and the absence of deceit are prerequisites for receiving this celestial honor.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,f rom Abu Gurra who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who visits his brother for the Sake of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> during an illness or well-being, neither coming to him for a deception nor for an exchange (reciprocal), Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Allocate seventy thousand Angels to him calling out behind his back:
‘You have done well, and the Paradise is (Made to be) better for you, for you are a visitor of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, and you are a delegate of the Beneficent’,
until he comes to his house’.

So Yusayr said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! And even if the place was distant?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, O Yusayr, and even if the place was at a travel distance of a year, for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is the most Benevolent, and the Angels are numerous. They would be escorting him until he returns to his own house’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu Ghirrah who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah saying, ‘If one visits his brother (in belief) for the sake of Allah, in his illness or in good health, not to deceive or to receive something, Allah will appoint seventy thousand angels to applaud behind him, “How beautiful is your deed! How beautiful is paradise for you! You are the visitor of Allah and the delegate to the Most Beneficent one.” This happens until he comes home.’

Yasyr then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, is it so even if the place of visitation is far away?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, O Yasyr, even if the place of visitation is at a distance of one year’s journey; Allah is generous and the angles are a great many. They escort him until he reaches his home.’”
